headline: Computational design of gene regulatory networks and biomolecular circuits
label: Gene Regulatory Network Design
summary: Three unreviewed preprints apply differentiable optimization, formal contracts, and reinforcement learning to program regulatory network function.
synthesis: The shared thread is the shift from analysing regulatory networks to specifying and optimizing them as engineering objects. jaxgrn applies differentiable programming to optimize thousands of gene regulatory networks end-to-end on GPUs, with stochastic simulation in the loop. The chemical reaction network abstraction derives polyhedral assume-guarantee contract specifications via monomial dominance in log coordinates, targeting compositional design of biomolecular circuits. REGAL instead uses reinforcement learning to program enhancer regulatory grammar against sequence-to-function oracles, aiming at tissue-specific enhancers across species. The new element is the combination of formal, compositional specification with simulation-driven and learned optimization. The items are heterogeneous: only jaxgrn explicitly treats stochastic dynamics. All three are unreviewed preprints, so these results remain provisional.
